probe.title: Your Page Title
probe.text_sample: Your Page Title Overview Buy Hemingway Magazine Fashion Design Music Culture Travel Podcast Latest: Making records slowly About Authors Membership Contact Sign in The tailor who refuses to hurry Sleeves you can read from across the room A record shop in Gothenburg arranges its racks by sleeve, not by genre. Sales went up. Erik Lindqvist 21 August 2026 , 1 min read Music Hands in a pale blue shirt flicking through a crate of colourful record sleeves. Walk into the shop and the first thing you notice is that nothing is filed by genre. The racks are arranged by sleeve: typographic covers on the left wall, photographs on the right, illustration in the middle. Buying with your eyes The owner started doing it as a joke during a slow winter. Customers stayed longer, picked up records they would never have found and, to his surprise, bought more of them. Designers as the draw There is now a small shelf by the counter for sleeve designers, with their names written on the dividers. Some people come in only for that shelf. It is a reminder that a record is an object first. You see it before you hear it, and in this shop, that order is the whole idea. Erik Lindqvist Erik Lindqvist edits the mu
